REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JANUARY 10, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
JANUARY 10, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Bishop David Montgomery, Church of Jesus Christ
  of the Latter-Day Saints – First Ward.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by City of Cerritos Recreation Services
  Division Youth Basketball Pee Wee Division team - Lakers.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Joy De La Paz spoke regarding updating the City’s parking permit program and
  a recent local newspaper article.

  Yanet Lindher spoke regarding updating the City’s parking permit program.

  Gail Grossman spoke regarding perceived actions of City Councilmembers.

  Mel Cortez expressed concerns regarding the City budget, a member of the
  Economic Development Commission, and a recent local newspaper article.

  Cresinni Tan spoke regarding updating the City’s parking permit program.

  Daisy Legasca expressed concern regarding communication at a recent City
  Council meeting and regarding an Economic Development Commission
  member.

  Erik Schulte spoke regarding the City’s parking permit program.

  Rich Gardner spoke regarding Alzheimer’s awareness.

  Christopher Craig, representing the Office of Assembly member Cristina Garcia,
  announced upcoming events.
 City of Cerritos  January 10, 2019

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Martin Grossman spoke regarding the annual Mayoral transition.

  Jay Gray spoke regarding perceived actions of City Councilmembers, a member
  of the Economic Development Commission and Alzheimer’s awareness.

  Jane Yim spoke regarding perceived actions of an Economic Development
  Commission member and a local newspaper.

  Sam Desai spoke regarding perceived actions of an Economic Development
  Commission member and a local newspaper.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke regarding Alzheimer’s awareness.

  Omkar Hanamsagar, Whitney High School student, spoke regarding enhancing
  learning technology in the classroom.

  Rebeca Carlin spoke regarding discontinuing delivery of a local newspaper.

  CONSENSUS (Pulido): Directed staff to evaluate opportunities to designate
  the City of Cerritos as a "Dementia-Friendly Purple City" and provide
  information regarding the City of Riverside "wandering" policy.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted
  by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  December 13, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of December 13, 2018
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated January 10,
  2019 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  1/10/2019  $11,062,432.65 (COUNCIL)
 City of Cerritos  January 10, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.1. (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated January 10, 2019 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  Successor Agency  1/10/2019  $  13,509.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the
  period ending November 30, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the period ending
  November 30, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business
9A.  Review and consideration of the potential for the Cerritos electric utility to
  serve residential customers (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ramzi Raufdeen, Electric Utility Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.
 City of Cerritos  January 10, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke regarding additional clarification of kilowatt or
  megawatt price per unit for each of the agencies (Magnolia, Edison, and
  market).

  Mel Cortez expressed support for any benefit for Cerritos residents.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1. Direct staff to finalize their review of service options to serve the City’s
  residents, including the option for residents to choose renewable power;
  and

  2. Authorize the expenditure of $50,000 toward legal fees and technical
  studies necessary for the required discussions with Southern California
  Edison, the California Energy Commission and any additional regulatory
  agencies; and

  3. Allocate funding from the approved legal services account in the 2018-19
  fiscal year budget toward the legal fees and technical studies (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5– 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of an informational report on the Property
  Preservation Commission’s review of the potential pine tree reforestation plan
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Laura Oglesby requested relocating the existing pine trees, as opposed to
  destroying them and recommended replacing the pine trees with Chinese
  Pistache, Long Leaf Yellow Wood, and Red Oak trees.

  Carissa Cordero expressed support for removal of the pine trees.

  Bryan Thornhill expressed concern regarding sap and pine needles from the
  pine trees and supports the removal of the pine trees.

  Jonathan Cordero suggested the City contact lumber companies in order to
  reduce the cost of the pine tree removal.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.
 City of Cerritos  January 10, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to file the
  staff report and continue to defer to the Property Preservation Commission for
  a final decision (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Cerritos Sheriff Station Captain Joe Nunez provided an update on progress
  made with regard to public safety and the homicide that occurred on the 91
  freeway August 17, 2018.

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Hu, and Yokoyama, Mayor
  Pro-Tem Solanki, and Mayor Pulido.

  CONSENSUS (Solanki): Directed staff to place an item on a future agenda to
  discuss a Request for Proposals process for all legal services.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 10:45 p.m. in memory of Amos Williams, Bruce
  Mulhearn, Nicolas Latz, and Satya Paul Jandial.

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
